title: Canonical unbounded proper direct-image comparison for finite coefficient extension
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes (each admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of rings satisfying the ascending chain condition on ideals) [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Work on the small ordinary etale sites in the entire derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $T=X,Y$ write $e_T^*=A_T\otimes_{R_T}^L-$ for derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $U_T$ for exact restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use the canonical tensor/pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the adjunctions $f_R^{-1}\dashv Rf_{*,R}$, $f_A^{-1}\dashv Rf_{*,A}$ of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], with counits $\varepsilon_R,\varepsilon_A$. For every $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ define the $A$-linear comparison
$$\beta_L:e_Y^*Rf_{*,R}L\longrightarrow Rf_{*,A}e_X^*L$$
to be the adjunct of
$$f_A^{-1}e_Y^*Rf_{*,R}L\xrightarrow{\sim}e_X^*f_R^{-1}Rf_{*,R}L\xrightarrow{e_X^*\varepsilon_{R,L}}e_X^*L.$$
The canonical direct-image composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies $U_YRf_{*,A}$ with $Rf_{*,R}U_X$. Under this and $U_Te_T^*C\cong A_T\otimes_{R_T}^LC$, the map $U_Y\beta_L$ is exactly the ordered projection morphism
$$A_Y\otimes_R^LRf_{*,R}L\longrightarrow Rf_{*,R}(A_X\otimes_R^LL)$$
of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection], including its two tensor symmetries. Consequently $\beta_L$ is an isomorphism. This is natural in $L$ and its normalization is the displayed counit transpose; no flatness of $A$ over $R$ and no boundedness of $L$ is required.

proof.text: Exact restriction of scalars reflects derived isomorphisms: its homology comparison identifies homology after restriction with restriction of homology, and restriction of module sheaves reflects isomorphisms. This is the generic exactFunctor_reflects_derived argument, applied to the actual sheaf restriction functor.

Prove the unbounded restriction/direct-image comparison invertible without claiming that restriction preserves K-injectives. Given an A-module K-injective I, an R-module K-injective J and a quasi-isomorphism j:Res I to J, choose an abelian K-injective replacement k of the underlying J. The module-to-abelian acyclicity theorem applied with A and R shows that f_*(Uj followed by k) and f_*k are quasi-isomorphisms. Two-out-of-three gives that f_*Uj is a quasi-isomorphism; exact conservative forgetting reflects this back to R-module complexes. The generic derivedSquare_isIso and unit_isIso_of_resolution_quasiIso constructions therefore show invertibility of the exact-derived mate. The underived_mate identity identifies its input with the sectionwise restriction/direct-image identity. Transport the two adjunctions along leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory using isIso_mate_transport; the resulting square is exactly scalarRestrictionPullbackIso. Its mate is scalarRestrictionDirectImageMap, which is therefore invertible on every unbounded object.

Use scalarPullback_tensor_compatibility to identify the restricted scalar/pullback comparison with the inverse-image tensor comparison and the specified coefficient pullback isomorphism. This is a separate compatibility result for arbitrary derived objects, coefficient homomorphisms and morphisms of schemes; it has no properness, finiteness or direct-image assertion.

Apply the generic restricted_mate_eq calculation. Transpose the composite sigma_Y inverse, U_Y beta, kappa and G_R sigma_X under F_R left adjoint to G_R. Naturality of the geometric counit, the counit equations for the two mates, naturality of chi and sigma_X, and the preceding pullback/tensor compatibility identify it with c_(G_R L) followed by tensoring the R-geometric counit. The actual homEquiv_symm_rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap formula and naturality of derivedTensor in the coefficient isomorphism identify that transpose with the projection morphism followed by direct image of the coefficient identification. Injectivity of homEquiv proves equality of these actual morphisms. Precompose with the specified symmetry at Y and postcompose with direct image of the specified symmetry at X; functoriality gives exactly the second conjunct, including both symmetries.

The existing unbounded finite-coefficient proper projection theorem makes the projection morphism invertible. Its specialization is isIso_rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap_of_finite. The preceding equality and invertibility of sigma, kappa and the coefficient pullback comparison imply that U_Y beta_L is invertible. Conservativity of exact derived restriction gives invertibility of beta_L. Finally mateEquiv_counit, followed by injectivity of the inverse adjunction Hom equivalence, proves the displayed counit-transpose normalization. This completes the first and third conjuncts and combines them with the second; the original statement and all its hypotheses remain unchanged.
